policy.rule: Every new Firestore collection that stores queue, job, lease, dispatch, retry, progress or recovery state must declare a read budget here in the same pull request that introduces it (M8, firestore-reads-program).
policy.surfaces: Python under backend/ (.collection, .collection_group) and TypeScript/JavaScript under web/ (db.collection, db.collectionGroup, collection(db, ...), doc(db, ...)).
policy.kill_switch: FIRESTORE_COLLECTION_BUDGET_GUARD_ENABLED=0 disables the guard for an approved rollback and requires FIRESTORE_COLLECTION_BUDGET_GUARD_DISABLE_REASON.
policy.note: The guard is diff-scoped: a collection or computed site that already exists at the merge base is grandfathered, so these lists start empty and grow one reviewed entry per new work-state collection. A grandfathered computed site whose literal namespace tuple grows keeps its site::expression key, so the guard also compares the enumerable collection family between revisions and requires a budget or exemption for each new member. Offline fixtures in .github/scripts/test_check_firestore_collection_budget.py prove both directions for literal and computed names on both surfaces, for computed-family expansion, and for Python collection_group_id.

entry_fields.collection: Firestore collection id, snake_case or camelCase
entry_fields.owner: lane that owns the collection and its budget
entry_fields.unit: unit of work the per-unit budget divides by (job, batch unit, active user-day, ...)
entry_fields.reads_per_unit_budget: positive integer, reads per unit of work
entry_fields.reads_per_day_budget: positive integer, reads per day at the expected volume
entry_fields.basis: measured (settled billing or a caller counter) or planning-bound (an estimate, never booked as a saving)
entry_fields.source: where the number came from: query, dashboard, or document
entry_fields.reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD date the budget was reviewed

dynamic_entry_fields.site: repository-relative path of the file that computes the name
dynamic_entry_fields.expression: the computed argument exactly as the scanner prints it (for example f'new_{stage}_jobs')
dynamic_entry_fields.collection_pattern: the collection family the expression can produce (for example new_*_jobs)
dynamic_entry_fields.owner: lane that owns the family and its budget
dynamic_entry_fields.unit: unit of work the per-unit budget divides by
dynamic_entry_fields.reads_per_unit_budget: positive integer, reads per unit of work for the whole family
dynamic_entry_fields.reads_per_day_budget: positive integer, reads per day for the whole family
dynamic_entry_fields.reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD date the budget was reviewed

budgets.unit: one explicit handoff/projection attempt (<=128 siblings), cold source page (<=100 rows), or recording cold erase attempt
budgets.source: SCA-1959 dark source planning bound: generic handoff cycle remains 9 reads with one attempt per phase. Typed projection adds a private view: guard reads 2n sibling docs plus authority/root/cursor; completion repeats the guard for the actual session and reads the sibling receipts/accounting, bounded by 7n+20 <=916 reads per attempt for n<=128. Retries/redeliveries are separately counted. Privacy/customer ledger/outbox reads belong to their respective families. tests/integration/test_jobstore_provider_projection.py counts actual direct reads for the two-sibling real projection path. No production selector: expected 0/day, existing 1/day sentinel only. Measured fleet/conflict/recovery/writer volume and a replacement reviewed daily budget remain required before activation; source delivery books no savings. Ordinary typed cold source adds 5 direct family reads per row/attempt (<=500/page); recording cold erasure reads authority/barrier plus <=399 original cold keys (<=401/attempt). test_jobstore_cold_sink.py counts the actual two-sibling direct-read paths (5 for one copied row; 9 for recording erasure). These planning counts reuse the existing 1000 bound and 0 expected production/1 sentinel per day; they are not a new funded budget or fleet qualification. All retry attempts/redeliveries count separately. Staging seal/verify reads one opaque marker per attempt; bounded cold erasure retains the existing <=399-key cap (<=401 family reads). Additional staging keys count toward that same cap and require paging beyond it; no numeric bound increases.

budgets.unit: conversation delete accepted behind a busy account gate
budgets.source: Read path in database/conversation_batch_purge_jobs.py + conversation_tombstones.accept_deletion: accept txn 3, due scans ~3, claim/begin/finish 3, tombstone 1, ~2 busy retries x 4; reconciler empty polls 1,440/day. Volume: prod Cloud Run request logs 2026-11-12 17:30 UTC onward, 1,021 phone cascade deletes in ~18 h (~1,400/day) as an all-accepted upper bound.

budgets.unit: one narrowing Commit plus one explicit reconciliation attempt
budgets.source: G2 Rev 3 section 3.0: 1 guard read per narrowing Commit and 1 per reconciliation attempt; conflicts require separately counted attempts. Production path is uninstalled/dark (expected 0 reads/day); 1/day is a sentinel bound, NOT a serving volume forecast or ramp budget. Q15 measured narrowing volume/conflict/reconciliation rates and a reviewed replacement daily budget are required before activation. Local synthetic tests do not count as production reads. No saving is booked.

dynamic.unit: one maintenance-leader sample at up to 100,000 fresh results per window per environment
dynamic.source: SCA-2012: two count aggregations per 60s per prod/dev leader; each costs max(1, ceil(index entries/1000)); 100,000 total and <=100,000 pending => 200/sample, 288,000/day/environment. Not a throughput cap; revisit budget if cohorts exceed this planning envelope. Normally empty/small windows cost 2/sample. Existing lease check adds <=1 metadata read per maintenance call outside this count budget.

dynamic.unit: one explicit recording projection transaction attempt
dynamic.source: Reuses the original intake receipt, never creates another intake family: one read per guard, at most two guards per customer transaction plus one accounting/preflight read. Retries/redeliveries counted separately. Synthetic two-sibling direct-read counter is in test_jobstore_provider_projection.py. No runtime selection or activation: 0 expected production reads/day, 1/day sentinel. Actual fleet/recording transaction volume and reviewed daily budget are gates before activation.

dynamic.unit: one explicit recording erasure transaction attempt
dynamic.source: Reference census only; this phase does not read or delete the original intake. One read is a conservative sentinel per attempt, not a new serving grant. Private view erasure reads at most 2n+1 private documents plus one queue authority, n<=128, within the existing 1000 handoff-family bound. Hold/gate/deletion-intent reads stay with their original families. Retries/redeliveries are separately counted. Production selection remains absent, expected volume 0/day, sentinel 1/day. Fleet and daily volume remain a reviewed activation gate; no savings booked. Census reference construction moved to the pure retained_manifest helper; construction itself performs no Firestore read. Existing numeric budget and original unique intake custody are unchanged.

dynamic.owner: pgfoundation / SCA-1959 dark original staging custody
dynamic.unit: one explicit recording staging seal or verify transaction attempt
dynamic.source: Actual original intake point read: one per seal or verify transaction attempt; reuses the existing typed-provider intake bound of 3, expected production 0/day and sentinel 1/day. Repair context stays solely in its original FS custodian. No new TTL or serving selector. Retries/redeliveries count separately; fleet and funded daily budget remain activation gates. Source delivery books no savings.
